clauses.anchor: Problem, report [#EX-203], sentence 2: "With all five candle flames lit and a tear delay of 2, an active vulnerable enemy standing next to the player can remain completely undamaged."
clauses.note: benchmarks/isaac-core/private/harbor/isaac-exodus-release-regressions/tests/suite/main.lua:503-544 lights the five candles through their GetData().IsLit/LitTimer fields, forces MaxFireDelay=2 every frame and requires at least one MC_ENTITY_TAKE_DMG hit and HP < 99 within 8 frames.

clauses.anchor: Problem, report [#EX-203], sentence 3: "At a tear delay of 4 ... the aura pulses every frame, roughly twice as often as the intended rounded interval."
clauses.note: benchmarks/isaac-core/private/harbor/isaac-exodus-release-regressions/tests/suite/main.lua:545-549 requires exactly 4 damage callbacks in an 8-frame window at MaxFireDelay=4 (the unchanged starter produces 8). The intended interval of 2 frames is only implied publicly by "roughly twice as often".

clauses.anchor: Problem, report [#EX-247]: "Ritual Candle's five flames, both Sundial orbitals, Astro Baby, and Lil Rune. Every companion should disappear promptly once its owning collectible is no longer held."
clauses.note: benchmarks/isaac-core/private/harbor/isaac-exodus-release-regressions/tests/suite/main.lua:552-580 requires all nine familiars to exist while held and none of the five variants five frames after RemoveCollectible plus a CACHE_ALL evaluation. The reroll path is not exercised.

clauses.anchor: Problem, report [#EX-327]: "A released ball must create that effect whenever it dies, even though the mitt is no longer raised."
clauses.note: benchmarks/isaac-core/private/harbor/isaac-exodus-release-regressions/tests/suite/main.lua:412-460,1049-1052 catches a projectile, waits for the release, kills the baseball and requires >= 1 Baseball Hit effect two frames later.

clauses.anchor: Problem, report [#EX-335]: "Existing gas must finish its own animation and cleanup without requiring an Iron Lung to remain alive."
clauses.note: benchmarks/isaac-core/private/harbor/isaac-exodus-release-regressions/tests/suite/main.lua:461-474 spawns a gas cloud with no Iron Lung in the room, starts "Pyroclastic Flow" and requires the entity to be gone after 240 frames. Only removal is observed, not the Fade animation.

clauses.anchor: Problem, report [#EX-342]: "Their collision must continue to be processed after the firing Headcase is gone."
clauses.note: benchmarks/isaac-core/private/harbor/isaac-exodus-release-regressions/tests/suite/main.lua:475-502,1020-1064 finds a lob through the mod-internal GetData().IsExodusLobbed marker, moves it onto the player with Height=4, removes the Headcase and requires red hearts to drop within three frames.

clauses.anchor: Task, sentence 2: "Preserve behaviour outside the reported paths."
clauses.note: 26 preserved cases pass in the unchanged starter. Most observe the composite's other reports, whose repairs the starter already contains, so a fix that breaks them is caught; nothing observes an item, trinket, enemy or character outside the composite's twenty reports.

clauses.note: No case checks API usage. A Repentance-only call shows up only indirectly, as a failure of whatever behaviour it breaks in the pinned v1.06.T1 process.

clauses.anchor: Notes, bullet 4: "Do not replace the mod wholesale or add third-party code/assets."

clauses.anchor: Problem, report [#EX-184]: "The Forbidden Fruit's earned damage disappears if the item is removed or rerolled."
clauses.note: benchmarks/isaac-core/private/harbor/isaac-exodus-release-regressions/tests/suite/main.lua:267-284 uses the item once, removes it with RemoveCollectible, re-evaluates the damage cache and requires the damage to stay within 0.05 of the held value. Only the removal path is exercised; a reroll is not.

known_issues: Internal-name coupling: several cases read or write mod-internal GetData() fields that exist in the starter but are not public contracts: ReturnChance (benchmarks/isaac-core/private/harbor/isaac-exodus-release-regressions/tests/suite/main.lua:671,691; a repair that marks an excluded split tear with ReturnChance=0 instead of leaving it nil fails deja_vu_split_guard although nothing returns), parentEnemy (benchmarks/isaac-core/private/harbor/isaac-exodus-release-regressions/tests/suite/main.lua:774), IsExodusLobbed (benchmarks/isaac-core/private/harbor/isaac-exodus-release-regressions/tests/suite/main.lua:1024,1053) and the candle fields IsLit/LitTimer (benchmarks/isaac-core/private/harbor/isaac-exodus-release-regressions/tests/suite/main.lua:513-514,530-531). A repair that renames or restructures these fields is rejected or cannot be driven by the fixture.

ritual_candle_cadence (benchmarks/isaac-core/private/harbor/isaac-exodus-release-regressions/tests/suite/main.lua:548) requires exactly 4 damage callbacks in 8 frames. The 2-frame interval is only implied publicly ("roughly twice as often as the intended rounded interval"); nearest-integer rounding of 4/3 gives 1 and keeps 8 hits, so only a ceil-like reading passes.

Order dependence: the thirty main-suite cases share one run and one player (benchmarks/isaac-core/private/harbor/isaac-exodus-release-regressions/tests/suite/main.lua:264-1009). State leaks forward (Forbidden Fruit's +0.99 damage is part of every later damage figure; Mutant Clover is silently replaced by Anamnesis before its reset guard; a pcall failure in any step emits GCB_FATAL and leaves every later case unobserved).

Shared game-log markers (private NOTES.md, Verifier design): results are parsed from unauthenticated `[GCB_CASE]` lines written through Isaac.DebugString into the same log the submission can write to, so outcomes are only meaningful under the honest-code assumption.

Process coupling: the secret-room process runs with continued=true as player_type=18 (James), inheriting the James process's run from Steam's in-memory cache (benchmarks/isaac-core/private/harbor/isaac-exodus-release-regressions/tests/test.sh:85-108). apocryphon_stats and blue_moon are therefore measured on James, who already owns The Apocryphon.

Launch harness: this task runs the frozen composite's three suites and test.sh unchanged, but the Hub mounts the task's own tests/run-game.sh over the image's copy. That script queues the launch request as soon as the offline Steam client proper is up, repeats an ignored request once, replaces a client that takes none (up to four starts per game process), and allows longer wall-clock budgets. It decides no case. The image's launch sequence left game processes unstarted on the congested host on 2026-09-23 (UTC); see NOTES.md.
